verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean tilts by cos θ where the paper tilts by sin θ'; the docstring of `expNormalizer` says so explicitly ("using cosine instead of sine (a translation of the angular origin)"). Recovery: put θ' = θ + π/2, so sin θ' = cos θ; the average is over one full period of a 2π-periodic function, which is invariant under translation of the origin (Mathlib `Function.Periodic.intervalIntegral_add_eq`, used in this same file at `normalizer_even`, NavierStokes/LoopVariance.lean:214). Nothing downstream uses the phase of the tilt, only its full-period averages, and the loop is reparametrized in φ later. The normalization (2π)^{-1}∫_0^{2π} and the domain of z (all of ℝ) agree exactly. I found no declaration anywhere in `SmoothLoop.lean` or `LoopVariance.lean` that uses `Real.sin` in the exponential family, and no formal lemma asserting the translation invariance of `angularMean`, so the sin→cos identification is a convention recovered outside the formal text.
